Dechristianization
dee-kris-chuhn-uh-ZAY-shuhn
noun
The decline of Christian belief and practice in a formerly Christian society; from de-, removal, and Christian.

📖 Biblical Definition

Dechristianization is the process by which a society once shaped by the Christian faith loses it—abandoning the worship of God, the authority of His Word, and the moral order of His law, until a culture that was nominally Christian becomes practically pagan. It is the modern West’s great apostasy: nations that once filled churches, swore by Scripture, and ordered their laws and calendars by the gospel now empty the pews, mock the faith, and order life as though God were not. Scripture knows the pattern. After Joshua’s generation died, there arose another generation which knew not the LORD, nor the works He had done for Israel; the fathers’ faith was not transmitted, and the children turned to idols. Where men do not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gives them over to a reprobate mind; a people is destroyed for lack of knowledge; and the day of Christ shall not come except there come a falling away first. Dechristianization is no mere statistical decline but a spiritual judgment and a spiritual battle. The dictionary names it as the apostasy it is—a forsaking of the fountain of living waters for broken cisterns that can hold no water—and answers it not with nostalgia for a lost Christendom but with the only remedy: the faithful preaching of the gospel, the catechizing of the young, and the recovery of the Word, by which alone a dechristianized people can be re-evangelized and revived.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The decline of Christian belief in a formerly Christian society; a spiritual apostasy answered not by nostalgia but by the preaching of the gospel and the recovery of the Word.

DECHRISTIANIZATION, the decline of Christian faith in a once-Christian society.

Abandoning the worship of God, the authority of His Word, and His moral law.

📖 Key Scripture

Jdg 2:10 — "And also all that generation were gathered unto their fathers: and there arose another generation after them, which knew not the LORD, nor yet the works which he had done for Israel."

Rom 1:28 — "And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient;"

Hos 4:6 — "My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children."

Jer 2:13 — "For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Dechristianization is dressed up as progress and enlightenment; Scripture names it apostasy and judgment—a forsaking of the living God for broken cisterns—answered by the gospel and the Word.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The error to name is the secular framing of dechristianization as liberation and progress—the casting off of faith celebrated as a coming-of-age, the emptying of the churches read as enlightenment. But Scripture names the reality differently. A people that forsakes the LORD has committed evil, exchanging the fountain of living waters for broken cisterns that hold no water; a generation that knows not the LORD nor His works has lost a treasure, not gained a freedom; and where men will not retain God in their knowledge, He gives them over to a reprobate mind and a society to its own dissolution. Dechristianization is apostasy and, often, judgment—not a brighter dawn but a deepening dark.

The principle to recover is the only remedy for a dechristianized people. The answer is not a wistful nostalgia for a vanished Christendom, nor a merely political reconquest of the culture, but the same means by which the gospel first conquered: the faithful preaching of Christ crucified, the diligent catechizing of children so that the faith is not lost in a single generation, and the recovery of the authority and sufficiency of the Word. A people is destroyed for lack of knowledge; a people may be revived by it. The church’s task in a dechristianized age is to re-evangelize it, trusting the Spirit who alone can make dry bones live.
